newsitem.title: USA: American Home buys Pharmacia product rights.
newsitem.headline: American Home buys Pharmacia product rights.

text.p: American Home Products Corp said Thursday its Genetics Institute Inc unit had bought the development and commercialization rights to Pharmacia & Upjohn's ReFacto product for the treatment of hemophilia A.
The product, recombinant Factor VIII, is in Phase III clinical trials in Europe and the United States.
Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.
Genetic Institute will continue clinical development of the product, with the goal of worldwide registration and marketing.
Pharmacia & Upjohn will perform development activities and will manufacture ReFacto for Genetics Institute. Pharmacia & Upjohn will also have rights to co-promote ReFacto in certain areas.
American Home said hemophilia A, a blood clotting disorder, affects about 50,000 individuals worldwide. The U.S. and European market for Factor VIII products exceeds $1 billion, it said.

Until recently, Factor VIII products to treat hemophilia A had been made from pooled human blood. Products made through recombinant technology make available the needed clotting factor without the addition of blood or plasma products, thereby eliminating the risk of blood-borne viral contamination, American Home said.
